title: Area from a determinant
intro: An FEA mesh patch has vertices at P₁(1.5, 2.0), P₂(4.0, 7.0) and P₃(6.5, 3.5). Its area scales the aerodynamic force vector applied to that patch, so it needs to be exact — not eyeballed off the mesh.
prompt: What is the area of the triangle, in square units?
debrief:
Δ = ½·|det [[x₁, y₁, 1], [x₂, y₂, 1], [x₃, y₃, 1]]|. Expanding: 1.5(7 - 3.5) + 4.0(3.5 - 2) + 6.5(2 - 7) = 5.25 + 6.0 - 32.5 = **-21.25**, so the area is 21.25/2 = **10.625 square units**.

The minus sign is the part worth keeping. Take the absolute value and you get area; keep the sign and you get **winding order** — which vertex ordering the triangle was given in, and therefore which way the face points. A GPU's barycentric test uses exactly this signed value to decide whether a pixel lies inside the triangle and whether the face is front or back; discarding the sign is how backface culling silently inverts.

And the degenerate case is a feature, not an error. If the determinant comes out **zero**, the three points are collinear and no triangle is bounded — in trajectory work, three telemetry points going collinear is an intercept path, which is why this determinant is worth computing even when you don't need the area.
